summary.text: The third law of thermodynamics says that a system's entropy approaches a constant value as its temperature approaches absolute zero.
For a perfect crystal of a pure substance that constant is zero, because at minimum energy there is a single unique arrangement of its atoms.
A consequence is that no process can reach absolute zero in a finite number of steps, and the law gives an absolute reference point for measuring entropy.

facts.label: Glassy systems
facts.value: Can keep some residual entropy at very low temperatures

facts.label: Reaching zero
facts.value: Impossible in a finite number of operations

facts.label: Crystal defects
facts.value: Some crystals form defects that leave residual entropy

items.prompt: A flawless crystal of a pure substance is cooled toward absolute zero. What happens to its entropy?

options.label: It rises to a large fixed value
It stays the same as at room temperature
It drops toward zero
It grows without limit

items.explain: The entropy of a perfect crystal of a pure substance approaches zero as the temperature approaches zero.

items.prompt: A sample of glass is cooled to nearly absolute zero, yet some disorder remains. Why?

options.label: It lacks a well-defined order, so a leftover entropy can remain
Glass cannot lose any heat once it is solid
Cooling adds disorder after a certain point
Glass is a gas that has not finished condensing

items.explain: Without well-defined order the system can lock into a non-minimal energy configuration, or have a non-unique lowest state, leaving a residual entropy.

items.prompt: A team plans to chill a sample to exactly zero kelvin by adding enough cooling stages. What does the third law say?

options.label: It works if the pressure is high enough
It works with enough stages, in finite time
It cannot be done in any finite number of steps
It works only if done without heat exchange

items.explain: No process can bring a system to absolute zero in a finite number of operations; it would take infinitely many steps or infinite time.

items.prompt: Why is the entropy of a perfect crystal exactly zero at absolute zero?

options.label: All of its atoms have left the crystal
It has only one lowest-energy arrangement
Entropy cannot be measured in a crystal
Its atoms vibrate faster than anywhere else

items.explain: Entropy relates to the number of accessible microstates; with one unique minimum-energy state, the entropy at absolute zero is zero.

items.prompt: Why can scientists quote an absolute entropy for a substance rather than only entropy changes?

options.label: Because entropy is always measured at room temperature
Because entropy never changes in a closed system
Because heat capacity is infinite at low temperatures
Because the law supplies a fixed zero point to measure from

items.explain: The third law gives an absolute reference point, so entropy of a closed system measured from it is its absolute entropy.

items.prompt: Someone squeezes a sample harder before cooling it. Will the entropy it approaches at absolute zero change?

options.label: Yes, it rises with more squeezing
Yes, it falls with more squeezing
No, the constant does not depend on such parameters
No, but only if the sample is a gas

items.explain: The constant value cannot depend on other parameters of the system, such as pressure or an applied magnetic field.
